title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
SpaceX’s acquisition of xAI and plans for space-based data centers is a major technology story. Waymo secured $16 billion for international robotaxi expansion, reflecting rapid growth in autonomous vehicles. Adobe’s shift to AI signals a broader industry trend. Avalanche raised $29 million for small-scale fusion power research.

Cybersecurity concerns escalated with allegations of Chinese government-linked hacking of Notepad++ and a coalition demanding a ban on xAI’s Grok chatbot due to concerns about nonconsensual content. Oracle is considering a significant job cut of up to 30,000 due to AI data center costs.

The conflict in Ukraine intensified with a major Russian attack on energy sites, and Iran signaled a willingness to negotiate with the United States. Israel reopened the Rafah border crossing for Palestinian patients, and Paris prosecutors raided X’s offices. Finally, Bill and Hillary Clinton agreed to testify before the House Oversight Committee regarding the Jeffrey Epstein case.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
The Overnight Market Brief – Pre-Market Edition for February 3, 2026, provides a market overview following yesterday’s risk-on performance on Wall Street, with the S&P 500 up 0.54% and the Nasdaq 100 rising 0.73%. Key macro indicators include a 10-Year Treasury yield at 4.287%, a declining US Dollar Index at 97.41, and a significant surge in gold to $4939.3, reflecting a flight to safety.

Overnight, Asian markets experienced positive momentum, driven by a US-India trade deal and strong Hong Kong retail sales, with the Nikkei 225 up 3.92% and Greater China indices rising. European markets adopted a cautious approach ahead of the upcoming ECB decision. US futures are currently higher, with S&P 500 futures up 0.28% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.54%, indicating a rotation into growth-oriented tech.

Investors are closely monitoring the ECB meeting, the potential unwinding of the yen carry trade, and the implications of the US-India trade deal. With a light economic calendar, market direction is expected to be influenced by these thematic developments and technical positioning, suggesting a path of higher resistance.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
Here’s a summary of the Post-Market Recap by AGI Era:

Today’s market action saw a mixed performance, with the US market showing resilience despite underlying weakness. The S&P 500 rose 0.54% to 6976.44, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.73% to 25738.61, and the Dow Jones jumped 1.05% to close at 38373.83. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a lack of strong conviction.

Sector rotation was a key theme, with Technology (XLK) leading the gains (0.95%) while Utilities (XLU) lagged (1.46%). This indicates a shift towards growth and risk-on assets, driven by expectations of continued economic expansion. The rising 10-Year Treasury Yield, though data unavailable, is a headwind for growth stocks.

The US Dollar Index (DX.F) strengthened by 0.60% to 97.44, fueled by a potential Fed nomination and manufacturing data. Crude Oil (CL.F) experienced a significant drop (4.55%) due to supply-demand dynamics.

Within the Magnificent Seven, Apple surged (4.04%), while Nvidia and Microsoft faced selling pressure (2.89% and 1.64% respectively). This highlights profit-taking and sector rotation. Venhub Global Inc. (VHUB) saw a dramatic surge in after-hours trading.

Looking ahead, investors will be closely monitoring the ISM Manufacturing PMI rebound and any commentary from the Federal Reserve, particularly regarding interest rate decisions.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary: Israel reopened the Rafah border crossing to Egypt, allowing a limited flow of individuals needing medical attention, following two years of closure. Simultaneously, Ukraine reported “real results” from Elon Musk’s restriction of Starlink access to Russia, citing drone attacks. In Nigeria, eighty kidnapped churchgoers were released after escaping captivity, offering a small measure of relief. Beijing criticized the Dalai Lama’s Grammy win, reflecting ongoing tensions. Costa Rica elected Laura Fernández, prioritizing crime reduction. The U.S. has indicated a willingness to engage with the juntas in Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger, shifting its foreign policy focus. Finally, Ghana suspended its citizenship process for people of African descent. These developments highlight ongoing conflicts, shifting alliances, and humanitarian crises across the globe.
